reuse.why: The tree's shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend (which already takes the enable flag and is used by all three weekend paths) is left untouched; the daily rule is coded inline in getNextDate and the helper is simply skipped for daily schedules.

duplication.why: The `take: isDailySkippingWeekends ? 7 : 1` + `filter(!d.isWeekend)` pair is written twice inside getNextDate (forward and reverse lookups).

placement.why: In the right module, but in one consumer instead of the shared weekend helper that getUpcomingDates and schedule-template also call.

scope.why: Small and focused on getNextDate plus tests, but leaves out the other paths that apply the weekend rule.

maintainability.why: The rule now diverges: getNextDate skips daily weekends while server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and schedule-template.ts still move them; frequency is read from dateCond.value rather than the parsed schedule data.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts wraps getDateWithSkippedWeekend in `if (!isDailySkippingWeekends)` and filters weekends itself instead of extending the helper

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated take/filter for forward and reverse lookups is literal, not disguised.

one_place.where: Only getNextDate implements the daily skip; getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (server/budget/schedule-template.ts) still call getDateWithSkippedWeekend and move daily weekend occurrences.
